content:
A week from Thursday, I am running a Lean tutorial for 30-40 undergraduates of varying backgrounds. I have to fill two 1.5-hour sessions separated by a half-hour break.

I plan to alternative between lecturing and having them do exercises. The easiest thing would be to have them click links and use live.lean-lang.org. How many users can that support at once? We can also set up our own servers if needed.

I feel like we would have heared more if 40 was a problem, but somebody like @Joachim Breitner might know more about the FRO infrastructure.

You can additionally use lean.math.hhu.de as backup to extend capacities. I believe that one by itself should have more than the required capacity

@Jeremy Avigad — it's definitely possible for 30-40 students to overload live.llo if they hit it at the same time and import Mathlib. If you're can use a pure-lean configuration like https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=lean-v4.35.0 (or at least avoid an import Mathlib) then live can probably handle it with not trouble, especially if you let me know when the tutorial is and I can keep an eye on the server in the background — though 40 people doing the same thing may spread the available cores a little thin.
